training_commands.tooltip: Live read-out of the sidebar Controller panel settings (mode + invert_vy) plus the fixed gamepad → command bindings. Ranges shown below are derived from the gain sliders on this node — sim and sim2real both read the same four numbers.
Forward velocity at stick=+1. This is ALSO the training sampler's upper bound on lin_vel_x — training and runtime read the same value. Keep it realistic for the robot's mechanical limits.
Backward velocity at stick=-1 (positive magnitude). Usually lower than forward for quadrupeds.
Yaw rate at |stick_x|=1 on the right stick. Symmetric.

Deployment-side stick → velocity curve. 'linear' = direct scaling (most common). 'deadzone' = ignore micro-jitter around stick=0 (production grade for worn sticks). 'exponential' = power curve for finer low-speed control. Training sampling is always uniform over the full range — the curve only shapes runtime UX feel, it does NOT change what the policy learns. Custom functions entry will be added later.
Absolute stick threshold below which the output snaps to zero. Above the threshold the curve is remapped linearly to cover the full gain range. Typical values 0.05–0.15 for worn sticks.
Power-curve exponent p in vel = sign(stick) × gain × |stick|^p. p=1 is linear; p=2 (squared) is the common 'fine low / aggressive high' feel; p=0.5 (sqrt) is the opposite.

Walk These Ways gait parameterisation. When ON, the policy obs vector gains 7 extra dimensions (gait_frequency, 4 per-foot phase offsets, body_height, step_height) and training samples them uniformly. Runtime CommandBus uses the preset table below for D-pad shortcuts with continuous interpolation between picks — a single policy covers walk / trot / bound / pace / pronk without discrete mode switching.
Foot stepping frequency range (Hz). Training sampler draws uniformly from this interval.
Commanded base height range (m). Policy learns to track heights in this interval.
Table of gait presets used by the runtime CommandBus as D-pad shortcuts. Click to open the editor; leave empty to use the bundled defaults (walk / trot / bound / pace / pronk).
Seconds between fresh command samples during an episode (uniform in range). Keep tight for policies that should hold commands; widen for randomisation.
Fraction of episodes that use the all-zero command (stand still) instead of a random sample. Forces the policy to learn stationary stance.
When ON, the deployment CommandBus clips incoming commands to the training range, protecting the policy from out-of-distribution stick input. Strongly recommended on.

play_ground_setting.tooltip: Pick a scene from the registry. Options are filtered by current training backend (SB3 / Isaac Lab) and robot family (quadruped / biped). Selecting a scene auto-writes scene_type plus any recommended defaults from the registry entry.
World gravity on the Z axis. Earth = -9.81.
Height-field amplitude for rough terrain. Ignored unless scene_type is 'rough'.
Maximum incline for rough terrain generator.
Enable terrain difficulty curriculum (rough terrain only).
Toggle heightfield ray-cast sensor on the policy observation. Backend-agnostic — Isaac Lab ships it out-of-the-box, MuJoCo will add it in a future pass.
Physics timestep (seconds). Formerly on IL Simulation Config.
Isaac Lab PhysX rigid-body contact budget.
Isaac Lab PhysX rigid-body patch budget.

joint_init.tooltip: Visual per-joint init angle editor. Opens a popup with one spinbox per joint sourced from the connected Robot node. Output feeds ActorSetting.joint_init.

robot.tooltip: Registered robot asset (from robot_assets registry). The ONLY editable field on this node. Everything below is a read-only information panel sourced from the selected asset — all user settings live on the paired Actor Setting node.

Flat table of detected asset files (MJCF / USD / URDF). The active file for the current run is marked with ✔. Click a Loaded row to override the automatic selection; click the active row again to revert to 'auto' (backend-derived).

Read-only structural view: every body of the selected asset with its auto-resolved IR role. Shows the complete joint/body list of the robot — single source of truth used by compilers and the Actor Setting node's contact body picker.

actor_setting.tooltip: World-frame spawn position Z (height above ground).
Which bodies emit contact-sensor readings. Click to open a multi-select picker sourced from the connected Robot node's body list.
How many past contact frames the sensor keeps in its history buffer.
Enable feet_air_time tracking for reward terms.
Actuator P gain (uniform across joints). For per-joint overrides use the JSON editor on the Actuator Config node (future).
Select which joints the policy action vector targets. Empty selection = all joints.
Scale applied to the policy output before adding it to the joint target. Lower = finer-grained control. Absorbed from the former IL Action Config node.
When true, the scaled policy output is added on top of the joint default posture. When false, it is treated as an absolute target.

physics_config.tooltip: MuJoCo physics integration timestep. Smaller = more accurate but slower. Typical: 0.001–0.004 s.
Policy step interval. Must be an exact integer multiple of sim_dt. E.g., sim_dt=0.002 → control_dt=0.02 gives 10 physics steps per control step.
Maximum number of control steps per episode before forced truncation. Overridden by TrainNode eval path when EnvAssembler.time_limit_override > 0.
Actuator control mode. 'joint_position' = target joint angle (PD-controlled); 'torque' = direct torque command; 'joint_velocity' = target joint velocity.

rewards.tooltip: Select reward modules from the registry, then tune weights with inline sliders. Registry switches automatically based on backend.
Exponential kernel std for IL tracking rewards (track_lin_vel_xy / track_ang_vel_z)

terminations.tooltip: Select supported termination modules from the registry, then tune each selected threshold with the inline slider rows. Registry switches automatically based on backend (SB3 vs Isaac Lab).

task_config.tooltip: Learning task template. Selects the overall task semantics and command interpretation.
'fixed' = constant velocity command each episode; 'sampled' = random command from uniform distribution; 'curriculum' = difficulty increases as policy improves.
Target forward velocity in m/s. Positive = forward, negative = backward.
Target lateral velocity in m/s. Positive = left, negative = right.
Target yaw rate in rad/s. Positive = turn left, negative = turn right.
Per-task step limit override. 0 uses physics_config.episode_max_steps. Set > 0 to tighten limit for this task without changing physics.
Fraction of eval episodes that must succeed for the run to be considered 'converged'. Used by EvalConfigNode.save_best_model logic and convergence reporting.
Enable curriculum learning. When ON, command_mode is automatically set to 'curriculum' and curriculum_schedule becomes active.
JSON schedule for curriculum progression. Keys are milestone names; values define difficulty ramp parameters. Active only when Curriculum is ON.

domain_rand.tooltip: Master switch. When OFF, all randomization is disabled and the environment uses fixed nominal parameters.
Body mass multiplier range [min, max]. At each reset, a multiplier is sampled uniformly and applied to all link masses.
Floor friction coefficient multiplier range [min, max]. Sampled per reset.
Motor torque limit multiplier range [min, max]. Simulates actuator wear and manufacturing variance.
Joint damping coefficient multiplier range [min, max].
Standard deviation of additive Gaussian noise applied to each observation element. 0 = no noise.
When ON, applies random force impulses to the robot base at regular intervals. Tests balance recovery.
Number of control steps between push events. Active only when Push Robot is ON.
Random push force magnitude range [min, max] in Newtons. Direction is uniformly randomized in the horizontal plane. Active only when Push Robot is ON.

Curriculum domain randomization: gradually increase randomization intensity from 0 to full scale over training. none = fixed intensity from step 0. linear = linearly ramps up. exponential = slow start, fast ramp. Implements ADR-style scheduling for better sim-to-real transfer.

Training step at which DR schedule reaches full intensity. Before this step, randomization ranges are linearly/exponentially scaled from 0 to the configured values. Active only when DR Schedule is not 'none'.
Static friction multiplier range [min, max] sampled per reset.
Dynamic friction multiplier range [min, max] sampled per reset.
Surface restitution (bounciness) range [min, max] sampled per reset.

base.title: Base Link
base.desc: Randomize mass of the floating base link (standard Unitree naming).

trunk.title: Trunk Link
trunk.desc: Randomize mass of the trunk link (Boston Dynamics / common biped naming).

body.title: Body Link
body.desc: Randomize mass of the body link (alternate root naming).

.*.title: All Bodies
.*.desc: Randomize mass across every body on the articulation.

domain_rand.tooltip: Target body (regex) whose mass is randomized by this event term.
Additive mass offset range [min, max] applied to the target body.
Interval range between push events (seconds).
Push velocity range along world X axis [min, max].
Push velocity range along world Y axis [min, max].
Initial base X position offset range [min, max] at reset.
Initial base Y position offset range [min, max] at reset.
Initial base yaw angle range [min, max] at reset (radians).
none = full DR from step 0. linear = ramp intensity from 0 to 1 between start_step and end_step.
Global training step at which DR activates. DR is OFF before this step.
Global training step at which DR reaches full intensity.

obs_action_config.tooltip: Named obs/action contract preset. 'custom' = free-form fields below. 'unitport_go2_v1' = 45-d (joint_pos+joint_vel+imu+command+prev_action, position control). 'community_go2_sac_34d' = 34-d (joint_pos+joint_vel+imu+command, torque control); matches sac_unitree_go2_mujoco. When a preset is active, obs_components and action_type below are locked to the preset values.
Observation vector components. Selected items are concatenated in order to form the obs array. Order matters: network input shape = sum of component dims.
Symmetric clip applied to raw obs values before normalization. ±clip_range. 0 = disabled. Prevents extreme values from destabilizing training.
Number of consecutive observation frames stacked to form the network input. 1 = no stacking (Markovian). >1 provides temporal context for partial observability.
Must match PhysicsConfig.action_type to avoid mis-scaled commands. 'joint_position' = target joint angle (PD control); 'torque' = direct torque; 'joint_velocity' = target angular velocity.
Scalar multiplier on raw policy output before sending to actuators. Adjusts the action magnitude without retraining.
Symmetric clip on scaled action output: ±action_clip. 0 = disabled. Protects actuators from extreme commands during early training.

env_assembler.tooltip: Number of parallel environment instances. Default 8 — suitable for most single-GPU setups. Increase to 32-64 for server training. n_envs=1 is generally unacceptable for robot RL throughput.
VecEnv implementation. subproc = SubprocVecEnv (separate processes, 5-10x faster for ≥4 envs, required for MuJoCo). dummy = DummyVecEnv (single process, useful for debugging or lightweight envs).
Apply VecNormalize to observations. Maintains running mean/std and normalizes each obs element. Highly recommended for most locomotion tasks.
Apply VecNormalize to rewards. Divides rewards by running std. Useful when reward magnitude varies widely; generally not needed for well-tuned reward terms.
VecNormalize clip bound for normalized observations. Applied after normalization. Ignored when obs_normalize is OFF.
VecNormalize clip bound for normalized rewards. Ignored when reward_normalize is OFF.
Override episode_max_steps for this env assembly. 0 = inherit from physics_config.episode_max_steps. Useful to set a shorter eval limit.
ActionClip wrapper: clips action values to [-x, x] before passing to the environment. Prevents saturated actuator commands. 0 = disabled (no clipping).
Monitor wrapper: wraps each env with gymnasium's Monitor to record episode reward, length, and time. Required for SB3 EvalCallback and reward logging. Disable only for headless benchmarking.
When ON, the evaluation copy of this env built by EvalCallback has all domain randomization disabled. Ensures eval is on the nominal env for fair comparison.

base_asset.tooltip:
scratch: train from random init.
resume: restore weights + optimizer state (continue a run).
warm_start_actor: copy actor weights only, reset optimizer (transfer learning).
Training asset ID from the registry (e.g. "sac_unitree_go2_mujoco"). Auto-filled when you click an entry in the Training Assets panel; you can also type it directly.
Relative or absolute path to the SB3 .zip checkpoint. Leave empty to auto-select the primary checkpoint for the chosen asset.

algo_config.tooltip: RL algorithm. PPO = on-policy (stable, good for locomotion); SAC = off-policy entropy-maximizing (sample-efficient); TD3 = off-policy deterministic (low-variance). Algorithm choice controls visibility of conditional params below.
Total environment interaction steps. Displayed with K/M suffix. Typical locomotion: 1–10 M for PPO, 0.5–2 M for SAC.
Adam optimizer learning rate. Typical range: 1e-4 to 1e-3 for PPO; 1e-4 to 3e-4 for SAC/TD3.
Mini-batch size for gradient updates. For PPO: must divide (n_steps × n_envs). For SAC/TD3: samples drawn from replay buffer.
Discount factor for future rewards. Higher = more far-sighted. 0.99 is standard for locomotion; 0.995 for tasks with sparse delayed rewards.
RNG seed for reproducibility. -1 = non-deterministic (random seed on each run).
'auto' = use CUDA if available, else CPU. Network training is device-bound; environments always run on CPU regardless of this setting.
Number of neurons in the first hidden layer of the policy network. Larger = more expressive but slower to train. Recommended: 256-512 for locomotion tasks.
Number of neurons in the second hidden layer of the policy network. Can be smaller than Layer 1 to create a funnel architecture (e.g. 512 → 256). Set to 0 to disable the second layer.
Non-linearity for all MLP hidden layers. 'tanh' is common for locomotion with SB3 defaults; 'relu'/'elu' often faster to train.
[PPO only] Generalized Advantage Estimation smoothing factor. 1.0 = Monte Carlo returns; 0.9 = more biased but lower variance. 0.95 is standard.
[PPO only] Number of environment steps collected per env before each gradient update. Total rollout = n_steps × n_envs. Larger = more stable but slower updates.
[PPO/SAC/TD3] Entropy regularisation coefficient. "auto" = adaptive tuning (recommended for SAC). 0.0 = pure exploitation. Higher values encourage exploration and prevent premature convergence.

[SAC/TD3] Gradient updates per env-step collected. '1' = auto-tune to n_envs at runtime (recommended: keeps GPU busy). Set higher (e.g. 4–16) on powerful GPUs for more training signal per sample. Set '-1' to let SB3 decide.
[PPO] How many times to reuse each rollout buffer for gradient updates. Higher = more GPU utilization per rollout. Recommended: 10-20 for standard PPO; beyond 20 may cause instability.
Learning rate decay over the training run. cosine = smooth annealing (recommended). linear = linear decay to 10% of initial LR. constant = fixed LR throughout.

[SAC/TD3] Soft target-network update coefficient (Polyak averaging). Default 0.005. Smaller values (0.001-0.003) make the target Q-network update more slowly, reducing Q-value overestimation and preventing reward collapse in locomotion tasks. Recommended: 0.002 for quadruped gait training.

[SAC] Entropy target for automatic temperature tuning. "auto" = -action_dim (e.g. -12 for Go2). For locomotion with dense shaped rewards, a less aggressive target like "-6" (= -0.5 × action_dim) maintains more exploration and prevents premature policy collapse. Use "auto" to start, switch to "-6" if training collapses.
AUTO: buffer_size = total_timesteps ÷ 10 rounded to 10 k (recommended). Manual: exact capacity. Re-click AUTO after changing total_timesteps to refresh.
[SAC/TD3] Number of random exploration steps before learning begins. Fills the replay buffer with diverse experience before the first gradient update.
Save a checkpoint every N timesteps during training. Checkpoints are written to runs/<run_id>/checkpoints/ and can be resumed via resume_mode=warm_start.
'scratch' = start fresh, ignoring any existing checkpoint. 'warm_start' = load the latest checkpoint for policy_id_out and continue training from that point.

Enable automatic rollback when reward collapses. When ON: the guard reloads the best saved checkpoint and reduces LR whenever rolling reward drops below collapse_threshold × best_ever for patience consecutive rollout-ends.

Fraction of best-ever reward below which a rollout counts as collapsed. Default 0.65 — rollback triggers when reward < 65% of best seen. Lower = less sensitive (fewer rollbacks). Higher = more aggressive intervention.
Learning-rate multiplier applied immediately after rollback. Default 0.3 — reduces to 30% for 20 rollout-ends while the buffer flushes bad experiences, then linearly recovers to the original rate.
Maximum number of collapse rollbacks before training stops. 0 = unlimited (train runs to completion regardless of oscillation). Set to e.g. 5 to prevent infinite loops.
Use Prioritized Experience Replay — samples transitions with high TD-error more often, so the policy learns from its biggest mistakes first. Only available for off-policy algorithms (SAC, TD3).
Exponent controlling how much prioritization is used. 0 = uniform sampling (no PER). 1 = full prioritization by TD-error. Default 0.6.

Importance-sampling correction exponent. Compensates for the bias introduced by non-uniform sampling. 0 = no correction. 1 = full IS correction. Typically annealed from 0.4 toward 1.0 during training.

eval_config.tooltip: Number of full episodes to run at each evaluation interval. More episodes = more accurate estimate but slower evaluation.
Run evaluation every N training timesteps. Smaller = more frequent monitoring (slower training); larger = less overhead.
When ON, evaluation uses the deterministic policy (no exploration noise / action sampling). Recommended for fair performance reporting.
Automatically save a checkpoint whenever the current eval mean reward exceeds the previous best. The best model is exported by ExportNode.
Fraction of eval episodes that must exceed TaskConfig.success_threshold to declare the policy 'converged'. Used for early-stop signals in Phase D.
When ON, renders and saves a video at each evaluation. Requires MuJoCo headless rendering and an available display/offscreen context.
Directory where evaluation video files are saved. Active only when Record Video is ON. Leave blank to use runs/<run_id>/videos/ auto-path.

export.tooltip: Bundle / checkpoint directory name. Must be set to a non-default value before training can proceed (SafetyReview blocks training when this is still the <NEW> sentinel). Final output path: projects/<workspace>/training/exported/<bundle_name>/ when overwrite is ON, or <bundle_name>_<version>/ when OFF.

ON (default): successive runs overwrite the same bundle directory. OFF: append a version tag so each run produces a fresh directory — the Version field below appears so you can bump it manually (v1 → v2 → …).
Version tag appended to the bundle directory name when Overwrite is OFF. Free-form string — users commonly use v1 / v2 / stable / demo. Hidden when Overwrite is ON.
Include policy.onnx in the bundle. Required for UnitPort deployment on real hardware via ONNX Runtime inference.
Include policy.pt (TorchScript) in the bundle. Enables C++ inference deployment and serves as a backup to ONNX.
Include VecNormalize running mean/std (normalization.pkl). Required for correct inference if obs_normalize was ON during training.
Every file the next training run will produce, with Open buttons and ⚠ 'Will Overwrite' tags on files that already exist. Auto-refreshes when bundle_name / version / include_* change.

Structured compatibility diff between the connected Start Point bundle and the current canvas (framework / action dim / decimation / joint order). Green ✓ = ok, ⚠ = warm-start will reindex, ✗ = not compatible. Same data SafetyReview uses for the S2–S5 blockers.

Which physics engine runs the trained brain during Review. MuJoCo is the fast default; Isaac Sim matches the training renderer 1:1. Review happens in a separate subprocess owned by the workspace. Newton is reserved for a future UnitPort release.

Which arena the trained brain is tested in. Decoupled from the training PlayGround Setting — most of the time you review a trained policy in a DIFFERENT scene than it was trained in. The dropdown is filtered to scenes that the chosen Review Engine can actually load.
Run SafetyReview and launch a review session. Any error-severity issue on the canvas stops the launch — see the red borders and log for details.

vis_check.tooltip: step_interval: open viewer every N training steps. episode_split: divide total training into equally-spaced vis checks.
Training step at which the first visualization milestone fires.
How many training steps between subsequent visualization milestones.
Total number of equally-spaced vis checks across the full training run. The interval is computed automatically from total_timesteps.
Number of full episodes to show per milestone. Close the viewer window after the last episode to resume training.
When ON the viewer runs the deterministic policy (no exploration noise).

il_observation.tooltip: Select observation terms from the registry. Order determines obs vector dimension layout.

il_policy_network.tooltip: Hidden layer widths for the actor MLP (layer 1 → 2 → 3).
Hidden layer widths for the critic MLP (layer 1 → 2 → 3).
Initial log-std for the Gaussian policy. Community default -1.0 (std ≈ 0.37). Larger values = more exploration noise.
Hidden layer widths for the AMP discriminator MLP (layer 1 → 2). Only used when an AMP PPO Trainer is present. Community default [1024, 512].

il_ppo_trainer.tooltip: PPO = vanilla RL. AMP_PPO = style imitation — requires a ReferenceMotion node upstream with consumer_mode in {'amp','both'} and reveals the 7 AMP-specific hyperparameter rows below.
PPO optimizer learning rate. Typical range 1e-5 to 1e-2.
Scale on the clipped discriminator reward.
Blend r = (1-l)*style + l*task. 0 = pure style imitation, 1 = pure task (AMP disabled). Default 0.5.
Two-sided label smoothing for the discriminator BCE loss.
Discriminator optimizer learning rate. Typical range 1e-5 to 1e-2.

slow_anneal.title: Slow Anneal
slow_anneal.desc: {start:0.75, end:0.3, over_iters:3000}. Gradually shift from style to task over 3k iters.

fast_anneal.title: Fast Anneal
fast_anneal.desc: {start:0.75, end:0.3, over_iters:1000}. Quick shift from style to task in 1k iters.

warmup_then_anneal.title: Warmup → Anneal
warmup_then_anneal.desc: {start:0.2, end:0.6, over_iters:2000}. Start style-heavy, ramp up task reward.

custom.title: Custom
custom.desc: Enter a custom JSON schedule via the editor below.

il_ppo_trainer.tooltip: Anneal schedule for task_reward_lerp. 'None' = constant lerp. Presets provide common ramp profiles. 'Custom' enables the JSON editor.
Enable multi-stage training pipeline. Each stage applies parameter overrides on top of the baseline config above. Stages execute in order with auto/manual advancement.
Define training stages. Each stage overrides specific parameters (training_mode, rewards, AMP config, DR, commands) and has advancement criteria.
How to save checkpoints at stage transitions. 'both' = save on advance + keep best per stage.

default.title: Default
default.desc: GO2 standing pose + Gaussian noise. No dependencies.

reference_frame_0.title: Ref Frame 0
reference_frame_0.desc: First frame of the Reference Motion clip. Requires a ReferenceMotion node.

keyframe.title: Keyframe
keyframe.desc: Named MJCF keyframe (e.g. 'home'). Falls back to default if not found.

init_pose.tooltip: How the robot is initialised at each episode reset.
Per-joint Gaussian noise (rad) added on top of the init pose. 0 = fully deterministic reset.
Override robot Z position at reset (m). -1.0 = auto (0.32 for GO2 default/custom; inferred from keyframe/ref-frame).
MJCF keyframe name. Only used when Init Mode = Keyframe.
JSON array of 12 joint angles (rad). Only used when Init Mode = Custom.
Probability [0,1] that a reset uses reference-state init when mode = ref_frame_0. 1.0 = always, 0.0 = never.

frame_0.title: Frame 0
frame_0.desc: Always use the first frame of the reference clip.

uniform_phase.title: Uniform Phase
uniform_phase.desc: Sample a uniformly random frame each reset (APEX-style kinematic RSI).

init_pose.tooltip: How to pick the reference frame for RSI. Only used when mode = ref_frame_0.
